extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office examiners; patent applicants and their attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on preparing Office actions and for applicants on how submissions and cited references are to be handled during patent examination (MPEP §707 and related paragraphs). Covers withdrawal of finality under transitional practice, examiner duties, citation practices, and procedural form usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality upon payment of 37 CFR 1.17(r)
rubrics_metrics.description: The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon the timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r). Upon the timely payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r), all previously unentered submissions, submissions filed with the 37 CFR 1.17(r) fee, and any submissions filed prior to the mailing of the next Office action will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicting amendments should be clarified for entry by the applicant upon payment of the fee. Absent specific instructions for entry, all submissions filed as of the date of withdrawal will be entered in the order filed. Use form paragraph 7.42.01 to notify applicant that finality has been withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of 1.17(r) construed as request to dismiss appeal (transitional 1.129(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Notice of Appeal and the appeal fee under 37 CFR 1.17(b) were filed prior to or with the payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r), payment of the 1.17(r) fee is construed as a request to dismiss the appeal and to continue prosecution under 37 CFR 1.129(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should treat such payment as dismissal of appeal and continuation of prosecution; forms 7.42.01/7.41.02 reference this effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsive submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) — shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: If, upon timely payment of 37 CFR 1.17(r), the examiner determines the submission is not fully responsive to the previous Office action, applicant will be given a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.02 should be used. The reasons why the submission is not fully responsive must be set forth. The shortened period supersedes the prior Office action time period and may be extended per 37 CFR 1.136(a). If an appeal was filed and the 1.17(r) fee is paid, the appeal stands dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a first action final after submission under 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A first action following a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) may be made final if all claims are drawn to the same invention claimed prior to entry under 1.129(a) and could have been finally rejected on the grounds/art of record if entered before entry under 1.129(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.03 when appropriate. A shortened statutory period of THREE MONTHS from mailing is set for reply; special rules if first reply filed within TWO MONTHS and advisory action timing; statutory period never extends beyond SIX MONTHS from mailing. See MPEP §706.07(b) and 37 CFR 1.136(a) for extension and finality conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second submission entitlement under transitional after-final practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the first-submission fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) has been previously paid, applicant is entitled to have a second submission entered and considered on the merits if filed prior to abandonment and prior to filing an appeal brief under 37 CFR 1.192; upon timely filing and fee payment, finality will be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate fee and entity status in form paragraph 7.41.02. No amendment resulting from payment may introduce new matter into the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132). This paragraph should NOT be used in a design or reissue application or reexamination proceeding; after two payments, subsequent submissions treated under after-final practice 37 CFR 1.116.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's duty to perform a thorough examination (37 CFR 1.104(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application, the examiner shall make a thorough study of the application and a thorough investigation of available prior art relating to the claimed subject matter. The examination shall be complete as to compliance with statutes/rules and the patentability of the invention, and as to matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoroughness extends to applicable statutes/rules, patentability, and form. Search and investigation must be adequate to support any rejection or allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of examiner's action and explanation of adverse actions (37 CFR 1.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant (or patent owner and requester in reexamination) will be notified of the examiner's action. The reasons for any adverse action or any objection or requirement will be stated and such information or references will be given as may be useful to judge the propriety of continuing prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure enough information/references are provided so applicant/patent owner can judge whether to continue prosecution. Use clear language specifying reasons for rejections/objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search requirements and optional reports
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978. Any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared at national examination upon specific written request and payment of the fee set forth in §1.21(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office does not require an international-type report to obtain a later refund; applicants may request/ pay for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of copending applications as commonly owned
rubrics_metrics.description: Copending applications will be considered owned by, or subject to obligation of assignment to, the same person if: (i) file records refer to recorded assignments conveying entire rights to same person; (ii) copies of unrecorded assignments conveying entire rights are filed in each application; (iii) an affidavit/declaration by common owner is filed stating common ownership and facts; or (iv) other evidence establishes common ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit/declaration may be signed by corporate official when appropriate. Use these criteria to determine common ownership for double-patenting or other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action and permissible limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder of invention, fundamental defects), the action may be limited to such matters before further action is made. Matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations are permitted where further action would be premature; do not raise form issues prematurely if claim unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to reject claims that are unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, or not considered patentable as claimed, the claims, or those considered unpatentable, will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which claims are rejected and provide basis; follow citation and explanation requirements for rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite best references and designate parts relied upon for 102/103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. When a reference is complex or shows inventions other than that claimed, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable; pertinence must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 103 rejections explain how a reference is modified or plural references are combined. Provide figure/page citations and brief comments when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on applicant admissions and examiner knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination) as to any matter affecting patentability and may also rely upon facts within his or her knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an Office employee, the data shall be as specific as possible and may be supported by an affidavit of such employee when called for; such affidavit is subject to contradiction/explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of third-party-developed subject matter under 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned or subject to obligation of assignment at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine ownership/assignment relationships before using such subject matter as prior art under 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection preclusion by statutory invention registration waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in any original application naming an inventor will be rejected as being precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed in the application and the statutory invention registration. Similar rule applies for reissue applications under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply statutory invention registration waiver rules and specify grounds when invoking this preclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation data requirements (patents, foreign patents, printed publications)
rubrics_metrics.description: If domestic patents are cited, their numbers, dates, and names of patentees must be stated. If foreign published applications or patents are cited, their country, numbers, dates, and names of patentees must be stated, and other necessary data to enable identification. If printed publications are cited, the author (if any), title, date, pages or plates, and place of publication, or place where a copy can be found, shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When only part of a foreign document is involved, identify particular pages/sheets. Give bibliographic information sufficient to identify and retrieve the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance should be stated when record unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record of prosecution does not make clear the reasons for allowing a claim, the examiner may set forth such reasoning; the reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be subject of separate communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant or patent owner may file a statement commenting on reasons for allowance within specified time; failure to do so does not imply agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 must indicate key action info
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the current first action procedure, the examiner signifies on the Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 certain information including the period set for reply, any attachments, and a 'Summary of Action' which is the position taken on all the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-326 (or PTOL-90 coversheet) serves as first page. Identify allowed claims and attachments; use form paragraphs 7.100/7.101/7.102 to conclude actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone interviews and amendment practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may indicate that a discussion with applicant's representative may result in agreements to place the application in condition for allowance and the examiner will telephone the representative within about 2 weeks. Resulting amendments may be made either by the attorney/agent or by the examiner as an examiner's amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extensive amendments are necessary it is preferable they be filed by the attorney/agent to reduce workload and provide a better record including applicant's arguments. Ensure parties are prepared for discussion (provide relevant attachments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments and referenced forms are part of the Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of references cited appears on a separate form, Notice of References Cited, PTO-892, attached to applicant's copies of the action. Attachments have the same paper number and are to be considered as part of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include PTO-892, PTO-948, PTO-152, and other relevant attachments as applicable; treat attachments as integral to the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include art unit number and examiner name in applicant replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to Office actions should include the 4-digit art unit number and the examiner's name to expedite handling within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expedites processing and ensures correct routing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific figures/pages/explanations when necessary for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary for adequate information, the particular figure(s) of the drawing(s), and/or page(s) or paragraph(s) of the reference(s), and/or any relevant comments briefly stated should be included. For rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103, the way in which a reference is modified or plural references are combined should be set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional cases (and pro se cases), more complete explanations may be needed to satisfy stringent requirements under 37 CFR 1.104(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of relevant prior art — explain relevance and consider IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art made of record and not relied upon is considered pertinent to applicant's disclosure. The examiner must consider all prior art references (alone and in combination) cited in the application or reexamination, including those cited by the applicant in a properly submitted Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.96 may be used as an introductory sentence. When such prior art is cited, its relevance should be explained in the Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited references furnished with Office action (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of documents cited by the examiner will be provided to applicant except where the documents: (A) are cited by applicant in accordance with MPEP §609, §707.05(b), and §708.02; (B) have been referred to in applicant's disclosure statement; (C) are cited and have been provided in a parent application; or (D) are U.S. patents which are cited at allowance (MPEP §1302.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of cited references are automatically furnished without charge with the Office action and placed in the application file, except as noted. For design applications, furnish relied-on sheets/drawing pages and first page of specification; other pages provided without charge; applicant may obtain complete copy through Copy Sales for a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for preparing and placing copies of cited references
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist in providing copies of references, the examiner should: (A) write the citation on PTO-892; (B) place the PTO-892 in the front of the file wrapper; (C) include in the file wrapper all of the references to be furnished and obtained from classified search file; (D) make two copies of each reference located elsewhere and mark one 'File Copy' and the other 'Applicant's Copy'; (E) turn the application in to Technical Support Staff for counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application handed in without required references will be returned to the examiner; missing references should be obtained and the file returned to Technical Support Staff as quickly as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and listing of parent-application references in continuation applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In all continuation and continuation-in-part applications, the parent applications should be reviewed for pertinent prior art. Where references have been cited during prosecution of parent applications and a continuing application (with no newly cited references) is ready for allowance, the cited references of the parent applications should be listed on PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no art is cited in a continuation application, list all references cited during prosecution of parent application at allowance. See MPEP §1302.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-submitted citations: do not replace examiner search obligation; not furnished with Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: MPEP §609 sets forth guidelines for applicants who submit prior art. Submitted citations will not diminish the examiner's obligation to conduct independent prior art searches or relieve examiners of citing pertinent prior art. Prior art submitted by applicant per MPEP §609 will not be supplied with an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat applicant-submitted citations as information but still perform independent search and cite pertinent art discovered by examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of listing references and recommendation to point out pertinent features
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing references for the first time, identifying data should be placed on PTO-892 attached to the Office action. No distinction is to be made between references on which a claim is rejected and those formerly referred to as 'pertinent'. It is recommended that the pertinent features of references which are not used as a basis for rejection be briefly pointed out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow recommended listing order and briefly state pertinent features for clarity and for printing in the patent when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of references later relied upon in subsequent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant in an amendatory paper refers to a reference that is subsequently relied upon by the examiner, such reference shall be cited by the examiner using PTO-892 unless applicant has listed the reference on a PTO-1449 that has been initialled by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper citation form is used when applicant-originated references become relied upon by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data used in citing references — classes, pages, IPC, and foreign conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing references, provide patent number, patent date, name of patentee, class and subclass for U.S. patents. For foreign patents, provide country, citation date, patentee, and U.S. class/subclass if appropriate; for IPC-filed groups cite IPC subclass/group/subgroup. If less than entire disclosure relied upon, include sheet and page numbers relied on and total number of sheets/pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §901.04 & §901.05(a) for series details. In cases where the entire disclosure is relied on, leave total sheets/pages blank. Use IPC subclass/group in appropriate examining groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication citation conventions (nonpatent literature)
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing a publication, sufficient information should be given to determine the identity and facilitate location. For books include author, title and date; for periodicals include title, volume number, date, and pages. Titles of books and periodicals SHOULD NOT be abbreviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as much bibliographic information as possible; minimal citations allowed only if complete details are unknown. Examples provided for books, parts of books, encyclopedia articles, handbook sections, and periodical articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include document identification and class/subclass for NPL with doc id
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a nonpatent literature reference with a document identification number is cited, the identification number and the class and subclass should be included on PTO-892.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: (S00840001) Winslow, C.E.A. Fresh Air and Ventilation N.Y., E.P. Dutton, 1926, p. 97-112, TH7653, W5, 315/22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain photocopy of original publications outside the Office and indicate filing class
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original publication is located outside the Office, the examiner should immediately make or order a photocopy of at least the portion relied upon and indicate the class and subclass in which it will be filed, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure copies are obtained promptly and properly filed for examiner and applicant access.
